blocks.explanation:
Two different functions (sine and cosine) of two different angles are equal.
To find: all values of \(x\), first in \([0, 2\pi]\), then the general solution.
Plan: write \(\cos 2x\) as a sine, bring everything to one side, turn the difference into a product with \(\sin C - \sin D\), and set each factor equal to zero.
steps:
Given: \(\sin 3x = \cos 2x\).
To find: the solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution.
Method: \(\cos\theta = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta)\) makes both sides sines. Then \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\frac{C+D}{2}\sin\frac{C-D}{2}\) gives a product equal to zero, and a product is zero only when one of its factors is zero.

Make both sides sines
\[\sin 3x = \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - 2x\right)\]
\[\sin 3x - \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - 2x\right) = 0\]
Why: \(\cos\theta = \sin(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta)\) (complementary angles). With the same function on both sides, one formula can join the two terms.

Half-sum and half-difference of the angles
\[C = 3x,\quad D = \tfrac{\pi}{2} - 2x\]
\[\dfrac{C+D}{2} = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[\dfrac{C-D}{2} = \dfrac{5x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Why: \(C + D = x + \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(C - D = 5x - \frac{\pi}{2}\); halving each gives the angles needed in the formula.

Write the equation as a product
\[2\cos\left(\tfrac{x}{2} + \tfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\sin\left(\tfrac{5x}{2} - \tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0\]
So \(\cos(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{\pi}{4}) = 0\) or \(\sin(\frac{5x}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4}) = 0\).
Why: \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\frac{C+D}{2}\sin\frac{C-D}{2}\). A product is zero only if a factor is zero.

Case 1: \(\cos\left(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0\)
\[\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\]
\[\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\]
In \([0, 2\pi]\): \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
Why: in one turn \(\cos\theta = 0\) at \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\); these are \(\pi\) apart, so all such angles are \(\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\). Multiplying by 2 doubles the step to \(2n\pi\).

Case 2: \(\sin\left(\frac{5x}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0\)
\[\dfrac{5x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = n\pi\]
\[\dfrac{5x}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + n\pi\]
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{10} + \dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\]
Why: \(\sin\theta = 0\) at \(\theta = 0, \pi, 2\pi, \ldots\), i.e. \(\theta = n\pi\). Multiply by \(\frac{2}{5}\) to get \(x\).

Values of Case 2 in \([0, 2\pi]\)
\[n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4:\]
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{10}, \tfrac{5\pi}{10}, \tfrac{9\pi}{10}, \tfrac{13\pi}{10}, \tfrac{17\pi}{10}\]
Why: each step adds \(\frac{2\pi}{5} = \frac{4\pi}{10}\). \(n = 5\) gives \(\frac{21\pi}{10} > 2\pi\), so we stop. Note \(\frac{5\pi}{10} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

Combine the two cases
\[\tfrac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi = \tfrac{\pi}{10} + \tfrac{2\pi}{5}(5n + 1)\]
Why: every value of Case 1 is already a value of Case 2 (take \(5n + 1\) in place of \(n\)), so Case 1 adds nothing new. The general solution is the single family \(\frac{\pi}{10} + \frac{2n\pi}{5}\). (Writing each of the five values in \([0, 2\pi]\) plus \(2n\pi\) gives the same set.)
